lessons: Split publishing from consuming. Publishing must be a module-level function (or a publisher class) that takes only state_dir and fs. It must never construct or read a Journal. Use uuid ids and an exclusive-create or temp+rename that never overwrites. Add a test that publishes with no Journal.

Wire the daemon hook for real: add a `control` callback to the DaemonTasks constructor and its callback tuple, update the test_daemon_tasks.py cases, and add a helper that builds ControlInbox from the daemon's lock-held Journal and fs. Leave test_daemon_composition.py unchanged.

Exactly once needs more than unlinking the file. After mutate succeeds, journal an applied marker keyed by request_id. On replay, skip mutate if the marker exists. Otherwise, check the hold again before a release. Test a crash after mutate but before unlink, and re-delivery of an identical file.

Make hold ids unique within the lifecycle. hold() should mint a fresh uuid, or reject any id already issued. Test this case: a release is published before its hold exists, then the hold is registered, then consume runs. The release must not be accepted.

Prove crash-safe publication with an injected Filesystem whose write fails after the temp file and before the rename. Assert that no <id>.json exists, consume makes no decision, and publishing the same id again is then consumed exactly once.

Earlier lessons said to keep the structure and fix only the findings. That produced narrow patches, and each review round found new design gaps. Before editing, re-check every Scope in clause against the diff. The re-entry branch also lacked the prior work, so confirm the base contents first.
reason: Checks pass, but review keeps finding design-level gaps: a second journal writer, no daemon wiring, exactly once not enforced. More capability should help more than another narrow retry.
